narratives.name: Automation Domain Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Automation Domain alpha matters for seller success in automation technology decisions.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers face fragmented automation practices with different teams using different tools for infrastructure, operations, network, and security automation, creating governance gaps, inconsistent practices, and inability to scale automation benefits across the organization.

The Automation Domain alpha tracks the maturity of Red Hat's positioning of Ansible Automation Platform as a unified automation platform that spans all automation domains, providing sellers with a structured progression from landscape assessment through strategy definition, tactic engagement, and technical validation to technology decision.

Sellers who follow the automation domain progression achieve higher win rates by establishing Ansible as the enterprise automation standard rather than a point solution, with expansion domains creating ongoing growth opportunities in additional automation use cases.

narratives.name: Automation TDP Practice Intent
narratives.description: The value narrative for the Automation TDP practice covering problem, solution, and outcome.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers face fragmented automation across infrastructure, operations, network, and security domains, with inconsistent tooling creating governance gaps, skills silos, and inability to scale automation beyond individual teams or use cases.

The Automation TDP equips sellers with domain-specific positioning for Ansible Automation Platform across four tactic areas -- enterprise-wide automation standardization, IT operations optimization, AI-assisted operations, and network infrastructure automation -- each with audience-segmented content, competitive intelligence, and structured conversation guides.

Sellers engage credibly in automation technology decisions by presenting unified platform capabilities, event-driven automation, and governance controls that address customer challenges across automation domains, converting technology conversations into qualified pipeline with measurable win rates.

narratives.name: Automate at Scale Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the enterprise-wide automation standardization tactic drives qualified pipeline.

narrativeContexts.context: Customers attempting enterprise-wide automation face fragmented tool landscapes where each team selects its own automation tools, creating governance gaps, duplicated effort, and inability to enforce consistent automation practices or measure automation impact across the organization.

The Automate at Scale tactic frames the customer's challenge around standardization and governance, then positions Ansible Automation Platform's unified controller, execution environments, and automation hub as the enterprise-wide automation standard that consolidates fragmented practices under a single governed platform.

Sellers who execute this tactic convert enterprise automation conversations into qualified pipeline by demonstrating how platform-level automation governance, content reuse, and multi-domain coverage address the root cause of automation fragmentation rather than adding another point tool.

narratives.name: AIOps Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the AI-assisted operations tactic makes AIOps achievable for customers at various AI maturity levels.

narrativeContexts.context: Operations teams are overwhelmed by the volume and complexity of infrastructure events, facing alert fatigue, reactive incident response, and inability to predict issues before they impact business services, while AI/ML initiatives remain disconnected from operational automation workflows.

The AIOps tactic positions Ansible Automation Platform's event-driven automation with AI-enhanced decision making as a practical path to intelligent operations, connecting AI capabilities to operational workflows without requiring a complete AIOps platform replacement.

Sellers convert AIOps conversations into pipeline by presenting an incremental adoption path that starts with event-driven automation and progresses to AI-assisted remediation, making AIOps achievable rather than aspirational for customers at various AI maturity levels.

narratives.name: Automation Competitive Position Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why automation-specific competitive intelligence drives evaluation success.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise automation decisions involve evaluating Ansible Automation Platform against alternatives including HashiCorp Terraform for infrastructure as code, custom scripts and homegrown tools, cloud provider native automation services, and vendor-specific configuration management tools, each with genuine strengths in their focused domains.

Terraform excels at declarative infrastructure provisioning, custom scripts provide maximum flexibility for unique requirements, and cloud provider tools offer deep integration with their respective platforms, but each alternative has limitations in multi-domain coverage, enterprise governance, or operational automation breadth.

Ansible Automation Platform provides a structural competitive advantage through multi-domain automation coverage spanning infrastructure, operations, network, security, and cloud, combined with enterprise governance controls, an agentless architecture that simplifies deployment, and an extensive content ecosystem that accelerates automation adoption.

activities.name: Assess Automation Landscape
activities.description: Evaluate the customer's current automation maturity and requirements across infrastructure, operations, network, and security domains.

given: Sales Play engagement has identified Automation as a relevant TDP for the customer

test.name: Automation landscape assessment verification
test.description: Verifies that the automation landscape is properly assessed when automation-related decisions are identified.
when: Customer conversation reveals automation-related technology decisions or challenges
then: Customer's automation maturity level is assessed and documented
Relevant automation tactic is selected from four options based on customer's primary challenge

narratives.name: Assess Automation Landscape Technique
narratives.description: How to evaluate customer automation maturity and select the appropriate tactic.

narrativeContexts.context: A customer's automation practices are evaluated across all relevant domains to understand current maturity and identify the most impactful automation opportunities.
The automation specialist assesses the customer's current tooling, practices, maturity level, and business case for automation using the Automation TDP's structured assessment approach.

Inventory existing automation tools, assess maturity across the ad hoc-to-enterprise spectrum, identify key automation domains, quantify the business case, and select the most relevant tactic from the four available options.
A clear picture of the customer's automation landscape enables targeted positioning of Ansible Automation Platform against their specific challenges and maturity level.

activities.name: Define Automation Strategy
activities.description: Design the enterprise automation approach and platform architecture with the customer.

given: Customer automation landscape has been assessed with maturity level determined

test.name: Automation strategy definition verification
test.description: Verifies that the automation strategy is properly defined when the customer agrees to explore Ansible.
when: Customer agrees to explore Ansible Automation Platform as the enterprise automation standard
then: Platform architecture is designed with controller, execution environments, and hub components
Governance model and automation KPIs are defined collaboratively

narratives.name: Define Automation Strategy Technique
narratives.description: How to collaboratively design an enterprise automation strategy with the customer.

narrativeContexts.context: After understanding the customer's automation landscape, the seller and customer collaborate to design a target automation strategy aligned to the customer's goals.
Design an enterprise automation approach covering platform architecture, content management, governance, tool integration, and measurable automation KPIs.
Present Ansible Automation Platform architecture options, map integration points with existing tools, establish governance controls including RBAC and approval workflows, and define success metrics.
A shared automation strategy document serves as the foundation for tactic-level engagement and technical validation.

activities.name: Execute Automation Tactic Conversation
activities.description: Deliver customer challenge-focused conversations using automation tactic-specific messaging, evidence, and audience-segmented content.

given: Automation strategy has been defined and specific tactic selected

test.name: Automation tactic conversation execution verification

when: Customer agrees to a topic-specific deep-dive on a specific automation challenge
then: Challenge framing resonates with customer stakeholders
Audience-appropriate automation content is delivered with engagement tracking
Competitive positioning against automation alternatives is established

narratives.name: Execute Automation Tactic Conversation Technique
narratives.description: How to deliver structured automation tactic conversations with audience-segmented content.

narrativeContexts.context: A customer has expressed interest in addressing a specific automation challenge, and the appropriate tactic from the four automation options has been selected.
Deliver a structured conversation using the tactic's challenge framing, audience-segmented content, and evidence to establish relevance and advance the automation evaluation.

Lead with customer challenge framing, present What to Say/Share/Show content matched to audience, share relevant customer references, and establish competitive positioning against automation alternatives.
Customer validates the automation challenge, engages with shared content, and the tactic conversation creates momentum toward technical validation of Ansible Automation Platform.

activities.description: Build and present competitive positioning for the automation domain including head-to-head analysis against Terraform, custom scripts, and vendor-specific tools.

given: Customer has identified competitive alternatives in the automation space

test.name: Automation competitive positioning verification
test.description: Verifies that competitive positioning is established when customers evaluate automation alternatives.
when: Customer reveals they are evaluating Terraform, custom scripts, or vendor-specific automation tools
then: Ansible differentiation is articulated on multi-domain coverage, governance, and agentless architecture
Competitive objections are addressed with evidence-based responses

narratives.name: Position Automation Competitively Technique
narratives.description: How to build and present competitive positioning for Ansible against automation alternatives.

narrativeContexts.context: The customer is evaluating automation alternatives including Terraform for infrastructure as code, custom scripts for maximum flexibility, and vendor-specific tools for deep platform integration.

Terraform excels at declarative infrastructure provisioning, custom scripts provide unlimited flexibility, and vendor-specific tools offer deep native integration, but each has limitations in multi-domain coverage, enterprise governance, or operational automation breadth.

Ansible Automation Platform provides multi-domain automation across infrastructure, operations, network, security, and cloud with enterprise governance, agentless architecture, and an extensive content ecosystem that competitors cannot match in breadth and flexibility.

activities.name: Validate Automation Technology Fit
activities.description: Conduct technical proof activities to validate Ansible Automation Platform for the customer's automation requirements.

given: Tactic engagement has generated customer interest in Ansible Automation Platform validation

test.name: Automation technology validation verification
test.description: Verifies that technical proof activities successfully validate Ansible for customer requirements.
when: Customer requests a proof of concept or technical demonstration of Ansible Automation Platform
then: Automation use cases validated with representative customer scenarios
Event-driven automation and multi-domain capabilities confirmed at target scale

narratives.name: Validate Automation Technology Fit Technique
narratives.description: How to conduct proof activities that validate Ansible for customer automation requirements.

narrativeContexts.context: A customer has engaged with automation tactic content and wants to validate Ansible Automation Platform capabilities through hands-on technical proof.
Design and execute a proof of concept covering the customer's priority automation use cases with clear success criteria aligned to their decision criteria.

Focus on multi-domain automation capabilities, event-driven response, governance and RBAC, and integration with existing tools, demonstrating with customer-relevant use cases and measuring against agreed criteria.
Technical validation confirms Ansible Automation Platform meets the customer's automation requirements at their required scale, providing evidence for the technology decision.

activities.name: Secure Automation Platform Decision
activities.description: Convert validated automation positioning into a customer commitment to Ansible Automation Platform.

given: Ansible Automation Platform has been technically validated for the customer's requirements

test.name: Automation platform decision verification
test.description: Verifies that validated positioning converts into a customer platform commitment.
when: Technical validation results confirm Ansible meets customer requirements and stakeholder consensus is building
then: Customer selects Ansible as enterprise automation standard
Subscription sizing and deployment plan are agreed
Expansion domains for additional automation use cases are identified

narratives.name: Secure Automation Platform Decision Technique
narratives.description: How to convert validated automation positioning into a customer platform commitment.

narrativeContexts.context: Ansible Automation Platform has been validated through proof activities and the customer is ready to make an automation platform decision.
Guide the customer through the commercial decision process, sizing the Ansible subscription appropriately and identifying expansion domains for future growth.

Present the business case consolidating technical validation results, competitive differentiation evidence, and ROI projections, then agree subscription sizing, deployment plan, and Automation Center of Excellence establishment support.
The customer commits to Ansible Automation Platform as their enterprise automation standard, with identified expansion domains creating a foundation for ongoing growth.

test.name: Automation competitive objection handling verification

when: Customer raises specific objections about Ansible vs Terraform, custom scripts, or vendor tools
then: Each objection is addressed with evidence-based responses from the automation battle card
Ansible's multi-domain and governance advantages are demonstrated in context

narratives.name: Handle Automation Competitive Objections Technique
narratives.description: How to address automation competitive objections with evidence-based responses.

narrativeContexts.context: Customers evaluating automation platforms raise specific objections comparing Ansible to alternatives they know or are already using, requiring evidence-based responses that acknowledge competitor strengths while articulating Ansible's advantages.

Terraform offers mature declarative infrastructure provisioning, custom scripts provide complete flexibility, and vendor-specific tools integrate deeply with their platforms, creating genuine competitive challenges that must be addressed honestly.

Ansible's multi-domain coverage, agentless architecture, enterprise governance controls, and extensive certified content ecosystem address the gaps in competing approaches, particularly for customers needing automation across infrastructure, operations, network, and security domains.

narratives.name: Engage Automation Tactic Customers Technique
narratives.description: How to deepen customer engagement through ongoing automation tactic conversations.

Deepen customer engagement through ongoing conversations, follow-up interactions, and engagement tracking to qualify the automation opportunity.

Monitor content engagement analytics, conduct follow-up conversations, use discovery questions to qualify automation scope and timeline, and establish cross-TDP connections if the customer's needs span multiple technology areas.
The automation opportunity progresses from initial interest to qualified engagement with documented scope, timeline, budget, and champion.

narratives.description: How to convert automation tactic engagement into qualified pipeline opportunities.

narrativeContexts.context: Automation tactic engagement has generated qualified interest with customer stakeholders aligned on the automation challenge and value proposition.

Create the opportunity in CRM with tactic attribution, build the automation business case with customer-specific ROI data, include relevant services and partner solutions, and document expansion automation use cases.
A qualified automation opportunity enters the pipeline with clear attribution, services positioning, and identified expansion domains for ongoing growth.

narratives.name: Frame Automation Tactic Challenge Technique
narratives.description: How to frame automation customer challenges in the customer's business language.

narrativeContexts.context: After assessing the customer's automation landscape, the seller selects the most relevant tactic from the four automation options and prepares to frame the customer's challenge.
Frame the selected automation challenge in the customer's business language, identify target personas, and draft initial messaging for both business and technical decision makers.

Review the selected tactic's challenge framework, customize the challenge framing with customer-specific data, identify the target personas and their specific concerns, and establish the connection to the Automation TDP and relevant Sales Plays.
The automation challenge is framed in terms the customer recognizes and cares about, establishing relevance before presenting the Ansible Automation Platform solution.
